findings.title: Unbounded numeric controls may publish a misleading 0..0 range
findings.message: Min and Max are always published as pointers for every Slider and NumberField. The Numeric bounds are described as optional. A control with no bounds set would then report a 0..0 range to the native accessibility tree, which assistive tech could treat as a fixed range. The reported range would also disagree with what ui.ClampNumeric actually enforces. This depends on how ui.Numeric represents unbounded controls, which is not visible in this part.
findings.suggestion: Set x.Min and x.Max only when the descriptor actually defines bounds. Otherwise leave them nil so they are omitted from the JSON. Use whatever 'bounded' indicator ui.Numeric exposes.
findings.evidence:
minimum, maximum := n.Numeric.Min, n.Numeric.Max
			x.Min = &minimum
			x.Max = &maximum

finding.message: The patch drops the old `ns == 0` guard (`glfw.GetMonitors()` returned nothing, so return early). `PollScreenChanges` now always calls `GetScreens()`, which rebuilds the native screen cache. During a transient zero-monitor state (sleep, display reconfiguration) the cache may be emptied or rebuilt incorrectly. `Window.Screen()` and the `Screen(0)` fallbacks would then get nil or stale data and could dereference it. The old code never touched the cache in that case.
finding.suggestion: Restore the early exit before rebuilding the cache: `if len(glfw.GetMonitors()) == 0 { return }`. Alternatively make `GetScreens` preserve the previous cache when no monitors are reported.
